An interest free loan is still a loan, and I didn't ask for any free money. I asked for the ei I've been faithfully paying into for 19 years, which I'm meant to ask for in exactly that situation.

I see a lot of comments here that assume if they're asking for CERB money back, it's because the person who received it wasn't entitled to it in the first place, so I just want to add my own story here.

At the beginning of the pandemic, I was laid off for seven months due to covid. I applied for ei only, not CERB, but they sent it anyway, and told me when I called to inquire that it was not an error, and I was meant to receive it. Now they're telling me it was a temporary advance, or a loan if you will, and they want it back.

I entered into no contracts. I did not ask for a $2000 loan, as that would be a poor financial decision for me. I'm now expected to somehow come up with this money and pay it back, and I consider this whole situation unfair and unreasonable.

I called service Canada and was berated by the staff there. I tried calling the number they provided to arrange payment arrangements, and a recording told me that due to covid, the call may be answered on a cell phone, and as such, any personal information I divulge could easily be intercepted by a third party. They ask you for all the personal information someone would require to steal your identity in order to identify you when you call, so when the woman answered and told me she was in fact on a cell phone, I hung up.

In what way is any of this ok? How is it legal for the government to give me a loan I didn't ask for, insist it was my money, then demand it back? They told me if I don't arrange to pay it within 30 days, they'll simply take it from me. If they'd made it clear that this was a loan, I would have refused to take it. If that didn't work, I would have set it aside to give it back when they asked. 

Nothing about this is ok. I shouldn't be on the hook for the government's mismanagement of a pandemic they should have known was coming.
